newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS Holding aims to be top Swiss bank.
newsitem.headline: CS Holding aims to be top Swiss bank.

text.p: CS Holding chairman Rainer Gut said in a newspaper interview that the Swiss financial group, which includes Credit Suisse, aims to lead Swiss banks in terms of profit.
Gut made no forecasts about near-term profits in the interview, which was made available to Reuters a day before publication in Saturday's Neue Zuericher Zeitung.

But he said a restructuring CS announced in July will allow it to increase profits in line with the increase in its balance sheet, which has taken place in recent years as a result of several acquisitions.

"With a balance sheet total of over 480 billion francs and a total gross income of about 12 billion francs annually, we stand at the top in Switzerland. Through the reorganisation we now also want to be number one in terms of profit," Gut said.
CS Holding also owns roughly 70 percent of New York- and London-based CS First Boston's capital.
In Switzerland, it has in recent years acquired Swiss Volksbank and New Aargauer Bank.
"It is true that we have won significant market share through targeted acquistions in Switzerland," Gut said.
He said CS Holding had paid between 4.5 billion and 5.0 billion Swiss francs for such acquisitions, raising it in stature from a number three position among big Swiss banks.
It is now considered the first- or second-largest Swiss bank, depending on whether or not only its banking arm is included, or taken together with its other holdings.

On July 2, CS Holding said it would set up four major business divisions. It will also reduce its workforce in Switzerland by 3,500 jobs over two to three years, included in a cut of 5,000 jobs worldwide. Gut said the bank hoped that no further job cuts would be necessary.
He also said he planned to remain as chairman indefinitely and said it was too early to talk about a successor.
"I feel comfortable in my work and don't think much of discussing a crown prince at the wrong time," he said.
